newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta to issue government stocks.
newsitem.headline: Malta to issue government stocks.

text.p: Maltese Finance Minister Leo Brincat on Monday announced three issues of Malta government stock, each of 10 million Malta pounds ($25.8 million).
The issues have a yield of 6.75 percent, 7.25 percent, and 7.8 percent, respectively, and mature in 2000, 2005 and 2012.
Applications will be received between May 12 and 24. The stocks will be traded on the Malta Stock Exchange.

The stock issues followed parliamentary approval of two bills allowing government to raise 100 million pounds to cover last year's deficit and to raise the limit on its overseas borrowing to 150 million pounds.
The previous limit, set in the mid-1980s, was 75 million pounds

Brincat said in parliament although the overseas borrowing limit was being raised, the government this year intended to borrow a total of 100 million pounds, including both local and foreign sources. Overseas borrowing would reach about 40 percent of the total.
Brincat said Malta expected favourable interest rates on long-term borrowing.

He said some 20 million pounds of the government's borrowing would go on a paper transaction to state-owned Malta Drydocks to enable it to clear outstanding debts, most of which are with the government through overdue income tax and social security payments for its workers.
